title: Bind authentication callback state to the browser context
verify: RED: In a disposable transport fixture, issue a valid provider state in browser A and call the callback from browser B or without the start cookie; the current path accepts the portable state and can proceed to provider verification/session issuance because no browser binding is checked.

GREEN: The start path issues the opaque server state together with a short-lived opaque browser-binding cookie; callback requires the matching cookie, rejects missing/mismatched/expired/replayed binding before provider verification or Identity & Access, consumes the binding once, and clears the binding cookie after the callback attempt.

VERIFY: Independently run the cross-browser, missing-cookie, mismatch, replay, and valid Telegram/Google callback matrix with injected provider doubles; compare provider-call counts and account/identity/invitation/session state snapshots before and after each rejection, then inspect cookie attributes and cleanup on valid/failed attempts.

evidence: The required full test gate failed only in the existing Admin invitation fixture because its callback jar did not retain the newly required start cookie; the task-owned browser-binding probe remained valid and the artifact is preserved as retry basis, not a production-path failure.
No task lifecycle, status, dependency, W9 record, or scheduler state changed at this historical gate.

The verifier-owned disposable browser A/B/empty-cookie probe passed 1 file / 5 tests; invalid bindings were rejected before provider verification with unchanged product snapshots, while valid Telegram/Google flows completed with one-use cleanup and the required cookie attributes.

Fresh npm run check, npm run build, focused auth/provider/Admin tests, full npm run test (21 files / 79 tests), and git diff --check passed after the bounded Attempt 3 fixture correction; the prior failure and all executor retry receipts remain preserved.

Independent adversarial review found no material semantic finding or operator-owned question across browser binding, provider/Identity & Access ownership, state preservation, cookie cleanup, privacy, and the W9 hard boundary.
The semantic artifact records SEMANTIC_VERDICT: semantic-pass; task identity, status, dependency, retry history, and lifecycle remain unchanged.

evidence_required: FT-001-AC-006 / REQ-001 / REQ-002 / REQ-014 / .memory-bank/contracts/authentication-transport.md#browser-bound-callback-state-and-bounded-retention RED: a valid provider state can complete from a different or cookie-less browser and reach session issuance; GREEN: only the browser that received the matching HttpOnly binding cookie can complete the callback, with one-use consumption and cleanup; decisive comparison: rejected callbacks do not invoke provider verification or mutate account, identity, invitation, or session state; artifact: .tasks/TASK-022-T3-FT-001-W10/ and .protocols/TASK-022-T3-FT-001-W10/.

FT-001-AC-007 / REQ-001 / REQ-002 / REQ-014 / .memory-bank/contracts/authentication-transport.md#invitation-acceptance-path RED: a cross-browser, missing-cookie, mismatched, or replayed invitation callback can reach acceptance or consume the invitation; GREEN: browser binding remains server-bound and invalid callbacks fail before invitation consumption; decisive comparison: invitation and session snapshots remain equal on rejection; artifact: .tasks/TASK-022-T3-FT-001-W10/ and .protocols/TASK-022-T3-FT-001-W10/.
purpose: Close the W9 login-CSRF/session-placement gap by binding provider callback state to the browser that initiated the flow.
success_outcome: A provider callback completes only with the matching server-issued browser-binding cookie; invalid, cross-browser, and replayed attempts fail closed before provider or Identity & Access completion and leave product state unchanged.
anti_goals: Do not replace the accepted process-local state store with SQLite, another durable store, a cache, or a multi-server mechanism.
Do not expose browser-readable authorization state, trust client role/center/account values, or add a development-login bypass.
Do not change provider protocols, Identity & Access ownership, membership writes, or any W9 task/history artifact.

stop_conditions: Stop and route to /spec-design if browser binding requires changing the accepted one-server modular-monolith + SQLite architecture, adding durable auth-state persistence, or introducing a new service/event/background worker.
Stop if the patch requires changing the provider verification contract or writing Identity & Access or Center & Scheduling state outside the existing public boundaries.
Stop if any W9 task card, protocol, execution evidence, semantic evidence, lifecycle, or retry history would need modification.

constraints: Reuse the existing five-minute authentication-state TTL and the existing foundation_session Secure convention: HTTPS requires Secure, local HTTP may relax it.
The binding cookie is HttpOnly, Path=/, SameSite=Lax, and has Max-Age no greater than the authentication-state TTL.
Negative callback probes use disposable state/DB fixtures, injected provider doubles, safe rerun, and state-before/state-after comparison; no live credentials or production database.
invariants: Provider callback state remains server-owned and opaque; the browser carries only the redirect state and opaque binding cookie.
A missing, mismatched, expired, or replayed browser binding cannot reach provider identity completion, invitation consumption, or session issuance.
A matched binding is one-use and its cookie is cleared after the callback attempt.
verification_targets: Existing FT-001 login/invitation regression / REQ-001 / REQ-002 / REQ-014: disposable HTTP/SSR cross-browser login and invitation callback probes for Telegram and Google with provider-call, cookie, session, invitation, identity, and account state observations.

FT-001-AC-006 / REQ-001 / REQ-002 / REQ-014 / .memory-bank/contracts/authentication-transport.md#browser-bound-callback-state-and-bounded-retention: compare cross-browser, missing-cookie, mismatch, expiry, replay, and valid callback behavior; verify invalid attempts stop before provider verification/session issuance and valid attempts preserve exact actor/session behavior.

FT-001-AC-007 / REQ-001 / REQ-002 / REQ-014 / .memory-bank/contracts/authentication-transport.md#invitation-acceptance-path: compare invalid browser-bound invitation callbacks with valid Telegram/Google acceptance; verify rejection preserves invitation/session snapshots and valid acceptance binds the exact account once.
